judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2, same grain) under the same Content Standard B6.1.2.6 'Demonstrate an understanding of integers' in Strand 1: Number / Sub-Strand 2: Number Operations, so the comparison is within one statement-type grain. The first (B6.1.1.6.1) establishes representing integers: its LCs are locating sets of integers on the number line, comparing with '< or >', and ordering them. The second (B6.1.2.6.2) is operational: its LCs are solving simple addition and subtraction problems involving integers (excluding subtraction of negative numbers). Fluency in placing and ordering positive/negative integers on the number line and judging relative magnitude substantively supports success in computing integer sums and differences, which depend on directional movement and relative position; the change is from representation/comparison to operation, not mere repetition. Same-rank direction is therefore lower-to-higher in demand from first to second, not a mandatory teaching sequence. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge/code context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading; the shared parent and weak code/page proximity signals were not treated as semantic evidence on their own.

Facility with factors, multiples, HCF and LCM therefore substantively supports success in finding common denominators for comparing, adding and subtracting fractions, justifying a same-rank developmental direction from the factors/multiples standard to the fractions standard rather than mere shared-strand overlap. Shared tokens ('demonstrate', 'understanding') and the weak B5.1 code prefix were not treated as evidence. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context (B5.1.1.3 is a merged duplicate-extraction node), so the judgment rests on the visible statement text and indicator labels only.
